mainTopic: The size of a חציצה, salt and water-drawing in the מקדש on שבת, and whether making sound is forbidden on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a כהן who wraps a hurt finger. A piece of cloth 3 by 3 fingerbreadths counts as a חציצה, but a small צלצול counts even when smaller because it is significant. According to רבי יוחנן, the משנה mentioned גמי in order to teach in passing that גמי heals. A new משנה then permits scattering salt on the ramp of the מזבח on שבת, and drawing water with a wheel from cisterns in the מקדש. The גמרא shows that salt differs from straw spread in a muddy courtyard, and works out how salt on the ramp avoids two problems: adding to the building and creating a חציצה. רבא publicly retracts a ruling about straw and teaches that it may be spread only with the bottom of a broken basket. The water wheel leads to a debate about making sound on שבת. עולא forbids even knocking, while רבה forbids only musical sound. Every source brought against רבה is explained another way, and the wheel is banned only in case a person waters his garden. אמימר therefore permitted the wheel in מחוזא, but the story begins to turn as the amud ends.

steps.title: The size rule: three by three fingerbreadths blocks, smaller does not
steps.stepSummary: A piece of cloth 3x3 fingerbreadths counts as a חציצה. Smaller than that does not. This matches what רבא said in the name of רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A piece of cloth three fingerbreadths by three fingerbreadths interposes. Less than three by three does not interpose. And this is the same thing that רבא said in the name of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a measurement rule for when a piece of cloth counts as a barrier (חציצה). It also notes that this is the same teaching as that of רבא in the name of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum size of a 'real' piece of cloth is 3x3 fingerbreadths. A piece that size is treated as a real object that blocks. A smaller piece is treated as insignificant, as if it were not there. This sets up the question in the next step, because רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא forbade a צלצול, which may be smaller than that.

keyTerms.meaning: They interpose. They count as a barrier (חציצה) between the body and what it should touch.
Three by three fingerbreadths. This is the minimum size for a piece of cloth to be significant.
Less than three fingerbreadths.
And this is the same as. It ties one teaching to another that says the same thing.

phrases.english: Three by three [fingerbreadths] — they interpose;
less than three — they do not interpose.
And this is what Rava said in the name of Rav Ḥisda.
phrases.notes: This fits a teaching from an אמורא that we already know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether a cloth on a כהן's body counts as a חציצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A piece of cloth 3x3 fingerbreadths or larger is a חציצה. A smaller piece is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This size rule is the yardstick for both questions that follow here.

steps.title: Does this size rule argue with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא forbade a צלצול as a חציצה. The size rule suggests a small one should be fine, so the two seem to argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this disagrees with רב יהודה, the son of רבי חייא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible conflict between the size rule it just quoted and the earlier view of רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא. It is setting up a question that will be answered in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא said a צלצול on the finger is forbidden because it is a חציצה, even if it is small. But the size rule says anything under 3x3 is not a חציצה. So it looks as if they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion that the גמרא usually goes on to reject.
It disagrees.
The son of רבי חייא.

phrases.english: Shall we say that it disagrees
with Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new size rule against an earlier opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the size rule fits with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא, who forbade a צלצול as a חציצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If anything under 3x3 is not a חציצה, then a small צלצול should be permitted. That contradicts רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.

steps.title: A small sash is different because it is significant
steps.stepSummary: There is no disagreement. A צלצול, even a small one, is a significant item, so it counts as a חציצה regardless of size.
steps.simpleTranslation: A small sash is different, because it is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no conflict. A small צלצול is an exception because it is considered an important item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 3x3 rule applies to an ordinary scrap of cloth. A צלצול is a made, purposeful item that people value, so it counts as a real object even below 3x3. The size rule therefore stays in place, and רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא is still correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. This introduces a distinction.
A small sash or band of cloth.
Significant or important. Because it is significant, it counts despite its small size.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a צלצול 'is not cloth' or that the 3x3 rule was cancelled. The rule still holds. A צלצול is simply an exception because of its importance.

phrases.english: A small sash is different,
because it is significant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggested disagreement in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק): a significant item counts even when small.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every piece of cloth under 3x3 is ignored, so a small צלצול would not be a חציצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A small צלצול is significant and counts as a חציצה. The 3x3 rule applies only to insignificant scraps.

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן, why didn't the משנה mention a small sash?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, a small צלצול on the finger should be permitted. So why did the משנה mention גמי instead of the bigger חידוש of a small צלצול?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן: instead of teaching us about a reed, let it teach us about a small sash!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the wording of the משנה according to רבי יוחנן's view. It wants to know why the משנה chose its example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן forbade a צלצול only because of יתור בגדים, adding a garment. A small צלצול is not a garment, and he does not use the idea that it is 'significant' as a חציצה, so it should be permitted. If so, the משנה could have taught the bolder case, that even a small צלצול is allowed, rather than the obvious case of a reed.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching us.
Let it teach us.
A reed, or reed grass. This is what the משנה allows the כהן to wrap on his finger.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
rather than teaching us about a reed,
let it teach us about a small sash!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא to רבי יוחנן's view and questions the משנה's choice of example.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to mention גמי, according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה normally teaches the greatest novelty. According to רבי יוחנן, a small צלצול is permitted, and that would be a bigger חידוש than גמי.

steps.title: The משנה teaches an extra lesson along the way: a reed heals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה chose גמי in order to teach, in passing, that גמי has healing properties.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us something incidentally: that a reed heals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה mentioned גמי on purpose, to slip in a side lesson that גמי is healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By picking גמי, the משנה teaches a medical fact: reed heals wounds. One might then worry about the rabbinic ban on healing on שבת. That ban is a rabbinic decree, and rabbinic decrees of this kind do not apply in the מקדש, so the כהן may still use it. The choice of example is explained without giving up רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter in passing. This is a side lesson taught incidentally.
It teaches us.
It heals.

steps.whatToRemember: The 3x3 rule holds. A small צלצול counts as a חציצה for רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא because it is significant. According to רבי יוחנן, the משנה chose גמי only to teach in passing that גמי heals.

phrases.english: A matter in passing
it teaches us:
that a reed heals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 about the משנה's choice of example.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Incidental teaching (מילתא אגב אורחיה): the example was chosen to convey extra information.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have used the bigger novelty of a small צלצול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה used גמי to teach that it heals. This is still permitted in the מקדש, since the rabbinic healing ban does not apply there.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common principle: a משנה may choose a less obvious example in order to teach a side fact.

steps.title: New משנה: salt on the ramp and drawing water in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits scattering salt on the ramp of the מזבח on שבת so the כהנים won't slip. It also permits drawing water from בור הגולה and בור הגדול with a wheel on שבת, and from באר הקר on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת, one may scatter salt on the ramp of the מזבח so the כהנים won't slip. One may also draw water with a wheel from בור הגולה and from בור הגדול on שבת. From באר הקר, one may draw water only on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists things that are allowed in the מקדש even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These actions would normally be forbidden by the רבנן on שבת. In the מקדש, however, the רבנן did not apply their extra restrictions, so these actions are allowed there. The rule about באר הקר is limited to יום טוב, and this amud does not give the reason for that limit.

keyTerms.meaning: We scatter or sprinkle
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
The Cistern of the Exiles, a pit of water in the מקדש
A wheel used to draw water
The 'Kar' well, a well of cold water

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ בּוֹזְקִין מֶלַח עַל גַּבֵּי כֶּבֶשׁ
phrases.english: MISHNA: One may scatter salt on the ramp
phrases.notes: The ramp leading up to the altar.

phrases.english: so that they (the priests) will not slip,
and one may draw water from the Cistern of the Exiles
and from the Great Cistern, with the wheel, on Shabbat,
and from the Kar Well on a Festival.
phrases.notes: Only on יום טוב, not on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בּוֹזְקִין מֶלַח עַל גַּבֵּי כֶּבֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the סוגיא about חציצה and גמי ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש on שבת, one may scatter salt on the ramp and draw water from certain wells with a wheel.

steps.title: Contradiction: salt only in the Temple, yet straw allowed anywhere
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא מפשרוניא tells רבא that the משנה implies salt may be scattered only in the מקדש. Yet a ברייתא lets someone scatter straw in a muddy courtyard, even outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא מפשרוניא raised a contradiction before רבא. We learned that one may scatter salt on the ramp so the כהנים won't slip. That implies it is allowed in the מקדש, but not in ordinary places. But a ברייתא says: if a courtyard was ruined by rainwater, one may bring straw and spread it there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made a point of mentioning the מקדש, so it suggests that outside the מקדש one may not spread material on the ground on שבת. The ברייתא, however, allows spreading straw over a muddy courtyard anywhere. The two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction between two sources
In the rest of the country, meaning outside the מקדש
And they contrasted it with another source
Straw
And he spreads it out

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אִיקָא מִפַּשְׁרוּנְיָא לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Ika from Pashronya raised a contradiction before Rava:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: בּוֹזְקִין מֶלַח עַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ
phrases.english: We learned: One may scatter salt on the ramp
so that they will not slip.
In the Temple, yes; in the rest of the country, no.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this from the way the משנה is worded.

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction: A courtyard that was damaged by rainwater —
one may bring straw and spread it in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אִיקָא מִפַּשְׁרוּנְיָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an inference drawn from the wording of the משנה in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the משנה that scattering material on the ground is allowed only in the מקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lets someone spread straw on a muddy courtyard anywhere. So why would salt be limited to the מקדש?

steps.title: Straw is different because it is not left there
steps.stepSummary: Straw is not meant to stay on the ground, so it is allowed anywhere. Salt is meant to stay, so outside the מקדש it looks like adding to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Straw is different, because a person does not intend to leave it there for good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing a difference between straw and salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person spreads straw, he plans to remove it once it has soaked up the water. So the straw does not become part of the ground. Salt, however, is left in place, so it looks like building up the ground. That is forbidden outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
He 'negates' it, meaning he makes it part of the ground and leaves it there for good

phrases.english: Straw is different, as one does not negate it.
phrases.notes: He does not leave it there as part of the ground.

steps.confusionAlert: Here מבטל does not mean 'cancel' in the usual sense. It means leaving something in place for good so that it becomes part of the ground.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (straw versus salt)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Straw and salt work the same way, so the משנה and the ברייתא clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Straw is not left on the ground, so it is allowed anywhere. Salt is left in place, so it is allowed only in the מקדש.

steps.title: What kind of salt? If it becomes part of the ramp, it adds to the building
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי about the salt in the משנה. If it is left on the ramp for good, it adds to the מקדש building, which is forbidden even on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא said to רב אשי: What exactly is the case of this salt? If the person leaves it on the ramp for good, he is adding to the building. And the פסוק says: 'All of it is in writing from the hand of ה׳; He made me understand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a two-sided question about the salt. This step gives only the first side and sets up the second side, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer said that salt is left on the ramp for good. If so, the salt becomes part of the ramp, and that adds to the מקדש building. The פסוק teaches that every detail of the מקדש was given through נבואה, so nothing may be added to it, even on a weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
He is adding
The building, here meaning the structure of the מקדש
Everything is in writing. The plan of the מקדש was given exactly, through נבואה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
This salt, what are the circumstances?
If he negates it, he is adding to the structure
(and it is written: 'All of it is in writing
from the hand of God upon me, He made me understand').
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א כח:יט. Every detail of the מקדש was set through נבואה.

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished yet. This is only the first side ('if he leaves it there'). The other side ('if he does not leave it there') comes in step 10.
steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מֶלַח הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דִּמְבַטְּלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the idea from step 8 that salt is left in place, and shows a problem with it in the מקדש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to scatter salt on the ramp, as explained in step 8 (salt that is left in place).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the salt becomes part of the ramp, it adds to the מקדש structure. The פסוק forbids any change to that structure.

steps.title: The other side of the dilemma: salt that blocks the feet
steps.stepSummary: If the salt is not given up as part of the ramp, it becomes a barrier (חציצה) between the כהנים' feet and the ramp.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he does not give it up as part of the ramp, it is a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the two-sided question from step 9. Now it shows that the salt is also a problem if it is NOT made part of the ramp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, salt that becomes part of the ramp was a problem because it adds to the building of the מקדש. Here, salt that stays separate is also a problem. The כהן's feet must touch the ramp itself during the service, and the salt sits in between. So both options seem to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrier between two things that must touch. Here it is between the כהן's feet and the ramp.
Giving something up so it becomes part of something else. Here, the salt would become part of the ramp.
It becomes / it counts as

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the second half of רב אחא בריה דרבא's question from step 9. The full question is 'either way it is a problem.'

phrases.english: And if he does not negate it (as part of the ramp),
phrases.notes: This is the second side of the question.

phrases.english: it constitutes an interposition.
phrases.notes: It separates the כהנים' feet from the ramp

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second horn of the dilemma begun in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to put salt on the כבש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt that is not given up as part of the ramp is a חציצה between the כהן's feet and the ramp during עבודה. Together with step 9, both options are forbidden.

steps.title: The salt is used while carrying limbs, which is not a service
steps.stepSummary: The salt is not given up as part of the ramp. It is only used during carrying the limbs to the ramp, which is not considered an עבודה, so a barrier does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is used when carrying the limbs to the ramp, which is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second side of the dilemma. The salt stays separate from the ramp. It is only there during a task where חציצה does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חציצה only ruins a real עבודה. If carrying the limbs to the ramp is just preparation, a barrier under the feet at that time causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the limbs of the קרבן
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
An official service in the מקדש

phrases.english: It is during the bringing of limbs to the ramp,
which is not a service.
phrases.notes: So a barrier at that time does not ruin anything

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חציצה problem raised in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a time when no עבודה is being done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The salt is under the כהנים' feet during real service, so it is a חציצה
steps.terutzMaskana: The salt is only relevant during carrying the limbs, which is not an עבודה

steps.title: Carrying the limbs is a service, based on a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer. The verse 'והקריב הכהן את הכל' is explained as referring to carrying the limbs to the ramp, so it is an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not a service? But it is written: 'And the כהן shall offer it all and burn it on the מזבח,' and the Master said: this refers to carrying the limbs to the ramp!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 11. It brings a verse showing that carrying the limbs to the ramp IS a real עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'והקריב' is explained as carrying the limbs to the ramp. Since the תורה writes it as part of the service, it counts as an עבודה. So a חציצה at that time would be a problem, and the answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is it not?' This introduces a challenge to what was just said.
But it is written. This brings a verse as a challenge.
The Master said. This quotes an earlier teaching.
And he shall burn (the קרבן on the מזבח)

phrases.english: And is it not? But isn't it written:
"And the priest shall offer it all
phrases.notes: ויקרא א:יג

phrases.english: and make it smoke upon the altar,"
and the Master said:
This is the bringing of the limbs to the ramp!
phrases.notes: So the תורה counts it as an עבודה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that carrying the limbs to the ramp is not an עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse, as explained by מר, lists carrying the limbs as part of offering the קרבן, so it is an עבודה.

steps.title: Change the example: carrying wood to the altar fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replaces the example. The salt is used while wood is carried up to the מערכה, which is truly not an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: during carrying wood to the מערכה, which is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the same idea as step 11 but switches to a better example. Carrying wood up for the fire is not an עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of step 11 still holds: salt may sit under the feet during a non-service task. Only the example changed, because carrying limbs turned out to be an עבודה. Carrying wood to the מערכה is not one, so the חציצה problem is avoided.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say. This corrects the previous answer.
Wood
The arranged pile of wood burning on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The salt on the כבש is not given up as part of the ramp, so it does not add to the מקדש. It is used only while wood is carried to the מערכה. That is not an עבודה, so it is not a forbidden חציצה.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
during the bringing of wood to the arrangement,
which is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by replacing the example from step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the case (אלא אימא) to a task that is truly not an עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The salt is used while carrying limbs, which turned out to be an עבודה
steps.terutzMaskana: The salt is used while carrying wood to the מערכה, which is not an עבודה

steps.title: Spreading straw in a rain-damaged courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבא taught that if a courtyard was damaged by rainwater, one may bring straw and spread it on the ground on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: a courtyard that was ruined by rainwater — one may bring straw and spread it there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבא. It allows spreading straw on a muddy courtyard on שבת, and it sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the idea from step 8. Straw is not meant to stay on the ground, so spreading it is not like fixing the floor. רבא states the permission without saying it has to be done in an unusual way.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught in public
Courtyard
Straw
Spreads out / scatters

phrases.english: Rava taught:
A courtyard that was damaged by rainwater —
one brings straw and scatters it in it.
phrases.notes: No mention of doing it in an unusual way

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about the straw case mentioned in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may spread straw in a courtyard ruined by rain

steps.title: A ברייתא says the straw must be spread in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא from a ברייתא. It says the straw may not be spread with a basket, only with the bottom of a broken basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But it was taught in a ברייתא: when he spreads it, he may not spread it with a small basket or a large basket, but only with the bottom of a basket!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבא's teaching. He quotes a ברייתא that requires spreading the straw in a different way than on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא seemed to allow spreading straw in the normal way. The ברייתא allows it only with a change (שינוי), using a broken basket bottom. So רבא's plain permission seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא. This introduces a challenge from a ברייתא.
A small basket
A large basket
The bottom of a broken basket. Using it is an unusual way of spreading.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava,
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
When he scatters —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְרַדֶּה לֹא בְּסַל וְלֹא בְּקוּפָּה,
phrases.english: he may not scatter it with a small basket or with a large basket,
but only with the bottom of a basket!
phrases.notes: An unusual way, not like a weekday

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's teaching in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's plain permission to spread straw
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows spreading straw only with a change (bottom of a basket), not in the normal weekday way that רבא's words suggest.

steps.title: רבא publicly admits his mistake about the straw
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the challenge of רב פפא. He publicly retracts his earlier ruling and teaches that straw may be spread only with the bottom of a broken basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רבא set up a speaker to announce his words, and he taught: What I told you before was a mistake on my part. The truth is that they said in the name of רבי אליעזר: When a person spreads the straw, he may not spread it with a small basket or a large basket. He may spread it only with the bottom of a broken basket.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא admits in public that his earlier ruling was wrong. He replaces it with the correct rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14, רבא allowed spreading straw with no limits. רב פפא challenged this from a ברייתא in Step 15, and here רבא fully accepts that challenge. The corrected rule still allows spreading straw, but it must be done in an unusual way, with the bottom of a broken basket, so that it does not look like ordinary weekday work.

keyTerms.meaning: A speaker who loudly repeated the rabbi's words to the large audience
"They are a mistake of mine" – a public retraction
However; but in truth
Spreads or scatters (the straw)
The bottom part of a broken basket

steps.whatToRemember: The final rule is that straw may be spread on שבת over a courtyard damaged by rain, but only in an unusual way: with the bottom of a broken basket, not with a regular basket.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a model of intellectual honesty. A great אמורא publicly announces that he was wrong, using the same public setting in which he first taught.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אוֹקֵים רָבָא אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: Then Rava set up a speaker over himself and taught:
phrases.notes: The speaker made sure everyone heard the correction.

phrases.english: The things that I said before you
are a mistake on my part.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: But this is what they said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
And when he spreads it, he may not spread it
not with a small basket and not with a large basket,
but only with the bottom of a broken basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי לִפְנֵיכֶם טָעוּת הֵן בְּיָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of רב פפא from Step 15 and corrects the ruling given in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Straw may be spread on שבת only in an unusual manner, with the bottom of a broken basket.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about drawing water from the Cistern of the Exiles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says one may draw water from בור הגולה using a wheel.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: One may draw water from the Cistern of the Exiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה to start a new discussion. This is a setup line that prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, people drew water from בור הגולה using a wheel, and a wheel makes noise. That detail is what leads to the next topic: whether making a sound is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One may fill, meaning draw water
The Cistern of the Exiles, a well in the מקדש area

phrases.english: One may draw water from the Cistern of the Exiles.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. Drawing the water was done with a wheel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the straw discussion and moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing water from בור הגולה on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: עולא curses a man who knocks on the door on שבת
steps.stepSummary: While עולא is at the house of רב מנשה, someone knocks on the door. עולא says this person is desecrating שבת by making a sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא happened to come to the house of רב מנשה. A certain man came and knocked on the door. עולא said: Who is this? May his body be desecrated, because he is desecrating שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that עולא held it is forbidden to make any sound on שבת, even knocking on a door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knocking is not music. Even so, עולא treats it as a violation of שבת. This shows his view that any deliberately produced sound is forbidden. The rabbis forbade sounds out of concern that a person might come to fix a musical instrument.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come
Knocked on the door
May his body be desecrated, a curse
Desecrates שבת

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to the house of Rav Menashe.
A certain man came and knocked on the door.
He (Ulla) said: Who is this?
May his body be desecrated,
because he is desecrating Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the noisy wheel in the משנה and raises the general question of making sounds on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עולא, producing even a non-musical sound, such as knocking, is forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: רבה says only musical sounds are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees with עולא. He says the rabbis forbade only a musical sound, not a plain noise like knocking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: The rabbis forbade only a musical sound.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back against עולא and says that knocking on a door is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה limits the rule to pleasant, musical sounds. Those are the ones that might lead a person to fix an instrument. A plain noise like knocking is outside the rule, so the man did nothing wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They forbade only
A musical, song-like sound

steps.confusionAlert: רבה (רבה) and רבא (רבא) are two different אמוראים. Here it is רבה.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא קוֹל שֶׁל שִׁיר.
phrases.english: They forbade only a musical sound.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָסְרוּ אֶלָּא קוֹל שֶׁל שִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the strict view of עולא from Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim of עולא that every sound is forbidden on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rabbis' decree covers only musical sounds, so plain knocking is not included.

steps.title: אביי brings a ברייתא about siphoning and dripping water for a sick person
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: on שבת, for a sick person, one may draw wine with a siphon and drip water from a dripping vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: One may draw wine up with a siphon, and drip water from a dripping vessel, for a sick person on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a source in order to challenge רבה. This is a setup step, and the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The siphon and the dripping vessel both make a steady, plain sound, not music. The words "for a sick person" are the detail אביי will use against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a תנאי source
A siphon for drawing liquid out of a barrel
A vessel that releases water drop by drop
Drip; let fall in drops

phrases.english: Abaye challenged him:
One may draw up wine with a siphon
and drip water from a dripping vessel
for a sick person on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against רבה's rule from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that only musical sounds are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits making plain water sounds only for a sick person, which suggests that for anyone else they are forbidden.

steps.title: Proving from the ברייתא that any made sound is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge. The allowance is only for a sick person, and the purpose is to wake him gently. So for a healthy person, making even a plain sound is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a sick person, yes. For a healthy person, no. What is the case? Is it not that he is dozing and they want to wake him up? Learn from this: making a sound is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes אביי's challenge. It shows that the ברייתא seems to forbid even non-musical sounds for a healthy person, which goes against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dripping sound is used to wake the sick person gently, without startling him. Since the ברייתא allows this only for a sick person, it seems that producing a sound is normally forbidden. Since dripping is not music, this contradicts רבה's rule that only musical sounds are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person
A healthy person
What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Learn from this
Producing a sound

steps.confusionAlert: The water is not dripped for the patient to drink. It is dripped so the sound will wake him gently.

phrases.english: For a sick person, yes; for a healthy person, no.
What is the case?
Is it not that he is dozing
and they want him to wake up?
Learn from this: producing a sound is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in Step 20 to complete the challenge against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that only a musical sound is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the ברייתא permits a non-musical waking sound only for the sick, producing any sound must be forbidden for the healthy. This supports עולא against רבה.

steps.title: The dripping water is meant to put the sick person to sleep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבה. The ברייתא is about a sick person who is awake. The dripping water makes a humming, musical sound that helps him fall asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is a sick person who is awake, and they want him to fall asleep. The dripping makes a sound like a humming melody.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אביי's reading of the ברייתא. It shows that the ברייתא does not prove עולא is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read the ברייתא as being about waking a patient with a plain noise. The answer flips the case: the patient is awake, and the goal is to put him to sleep. That calls for a melodious, humming sound, which is exactly the musical kind of sound רבה agrees is forbidden for a healthy person, so the ברייתא fits רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: who is awake
that he should fall asleep
humming or melodious sounds

phrases.english: No: it refers to a sick person who is awake,
and they want him to fall asleep —
so the dripping sounds like a humming melody.
phrases.notes: A musical-type sound, which רבה also forbids for a healthy person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 20-21 by redefining the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about gently waking a sick person with a plain noise, so a healthy person may not make even a plain noise.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about putting an awake patient to sleep with a musical humming sound, which fits רבה's view.

steps.title: אביי challenges again from guarding crops
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. A person may guard his crops from birds and animals on שבת, but he may not clap, slap, or stamp his feet the way he does on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבה: One who guards his fruit from birds or his gourds from animals may guard them in his usual way on שבת. But he may not clap, slap, or dance the way people do on weekdays.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new source against רבה. Clapping, slapping, and stamping make plain noises, not music, yet the ברייתא forbids them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These actions make plain noises, not musical ones. If they are forbidden on שבת, that seems to support עולא, who forbids any sound. The גמרא spells out this reasoning in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged him (from a ברייתא)
clap his hands
slap his hands against his body
dance or stamp his feet
on a weekday

phrases.english: He challenged him: One who guards his produce from birds,
or his gourds from wild animals —
may guard them in his usual way on Shabbat,
as long as he does not clap,
or slap, or dance,
the way people do on weekdays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, אביי brings a second ברייתא against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that only musical sounds are forbidden on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids clapping and stamping, which make plain noises. That suggests every sound is forbidden, as עולא said.

steps.title: Spelling out why clapping would be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason for the ban is. It suggests the reason is that clapping produces a sound, and producing any sound is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Is it not because he produces a sound, and producing any sound is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the logic behind אביי's challenge outright. This sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never gives a reason for its ban. The גמרא proposes the obvious one, that any sound is forbidden, which would match עולא and contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
is it not (introduces a suggested reason)
producing a sound

phrases.english: What is the reason —
is it not because he produces a sound,
and any production of a sound is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ברייתא quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for the ban is the sound itself, then plain sounds are forbidden, against רבה.

steps.title: The ban is a safeguard against picking up a pebble
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that the reason is not the noise. It is a rabbinic safeguard, so the person will not pick up a pebble to throw at the birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It is a rabbinic decree, in case he picks up a pebble.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different reason for the ban, which saves רבה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person shoos birds the weekday way, he may also do what he does on weekdays and grab a stone to throw. A stone is מוקצה and may not be handled on שבת. So the ban comes from a separate concern, not from the noise, and the ברייתא no longer proves עולא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic safeguard decree
lest, in case
a pebble

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that clapping is fine because the ban fell away. Clapping is still forbidden. Only the reason changed: it is a safeguard about the pebble, not a rule about noise.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
It is a decree, lest he pick up a pebble.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִטּוֹל צְרוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 23-24 by giving a different reason for the ban.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Clapping is forbidden because it makes a sound.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clapping is forbidden as a safeguard against picking up a pebble, which is מוקצה. It says nothing about plain sounds.

steps.title: New challenge: women playing with nuts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב's ruling that women may not play with nuts on שבת. It suggests the reason is the knocking sound, which would again mean every sound is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Women who play with nuts are forbidden to do so. What is the reason? Is it not because they produce a sound, and producing any sound is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another challenge to רבה, this time from רב's ruling about a game with nuts. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rolling nuts so they knock into each other makes a plain clicking noise, not music. Here there is no pebble to explain the ban. If the noise is the reason, עולא seems right that every sound is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: but then, what about (opens a new challenge)
playing
nuts

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Women who play with nuts — it is forbidden.
What is the reason —
is it not because it produces a sound,
and any production of a sound is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the crop-guarding challenge is answered, the גמרא raises a new source against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that only musical sounds are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nut game makes only a plain knocking sound, yet רב forbids it. With no pebble concern here, the noise itself seems to be the reason, which supports עולא.

steps.title: Nuts are banned because players might level holes, not because of noise
steps.stepSummary: The ban on women playing with nuts is not about the knocking sound. The worry is that they will level out holes in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The reason is that perhaps they will come to level holes in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from step 26 that the nut game is banned because of its noise. It gives a different reason: the players might fill in holes to make the ground smooth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nut game is played on the ground, and small holes get in the way of the rolling nuts. Players may smooth these holes over, and doing that on שבת is a form of בונה (building). So the ban is a safeguard against building, and it says nothing against making sound.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps he will come to (do something forbidden)
To level / to make even
Holes or pits in the ground

phrases.english: No, perhaps they will come
to level holes.
phrases.notes: Filling in holes in the ground counts as building, which is forbidden on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב's ban on playing with nuts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ban (a rabbinic safeguard).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The nut game is banned because the knocking makes a sound.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nut game is banned because the players might level holes, which is building.

steps.title: Proof from apples, which make no sound
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה bans playing with apples even though apples make no noise. So the reason must be leveling holes, and the same reason explains the nuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you do not say this, what about רב יהודה's ruling that women playing with apples is forbidden? What sound is made there? Rather, the reason must be that they might come to level holes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the answer from step 27 by pointing to a similar ban on playing with apples. Apples make no noise when they bump each other, so noise cannot be the reason for that ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If noise were the reason for banning the nut game, we could not explain why the apple game is also banned. The only reason that fits both games is the fear of leveling holes. This shows that 'leveling holes' is the true reason, and that the nut ban says nothing against making sound.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (a formula used to bring a proof)
Apples
Producing a sound

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
what about that which Rav Yehuda said:
Women who play with apples, it is forbidden,
there, what production of sound is there?!
phrases.notes: Apples do not make noise when they hit each other.

phrases.english: Rather: perhaps they will come
to level holes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 27 with a parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on playing with nuts is about leveling holes, not about noise.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's ruling banning women from playing with apples, a game with no noise.
steps.whatToRemember: Both games (nuts and apples) are banned for one reason: the fear of leveling holes in the ground. Noise has nothing to do with it.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about the water wheel
steps.stepSummary: A משנה allows drawing water with a wheel on שבת only in the מקדש. The גמרא suggests that the wheel's noise is why it is forbidden elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: One may draw water from the Cistern of the Exiles and from the Great Cistern with a wheel on שבת. In the מקדש, yes; in the rest of the country, no. What is the reason? Is it not because the wheel produces a sound, which is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against the view that sound is permitted. It uses a משנה that allows the water wheel only in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits the wheel in the מקדש, which implies that it is forbidden everywhere else. The squeaking wheel makes noise, so the גמרא suggests that noise is the reason for the ban. Then the rule of שבות (rabbinic bans) not applying in the מקדש would explain why it is allowed there.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
The Cistern of the Exiles (a cistern in the Temple courtyard)
The Great Cistern
A wheel (a pulley for drawing water)
The country, meaning anywhere outside the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself only says the wheel is allowed in these cisterns. The rule 'in the מקדש yes, elsewhere no' is the גמרא's inference from the משנה.

phrases.english: We learned: One may draw water from the Cistern of the Exiles
and from the Great Cistern
by the wheel on Shabbat,
in the Temple, yes,
in the country, no.
What is the reason?
Is it not because it produces a sound, and that is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the nuts challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new challenge from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule (step 19) that only a musical sound is forbidden, so producing a plain sound is permitted on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Outside the מקדש, the wheel is forbidden. The obvious difference is its noise, so making sound must be forbidden.

steps.title: The wheel is banned so a person will not water his garden
steps.stepSummary: The ban on the wheel is a גזירה. Since the wheel draws a lot of water, a person might use it to water his garden or his ruin.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a decree, lest he draw water for his garden and for his ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the wheel is banned because of noise. It gives a different reason: the wheel might lead a person to water his garden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wheel brings up large amounts of water easily. Once a person is using it, he may draw extra water for his garden, and watering plants is a forbidden מלאכה. In the מקדש this worry does not apply, so the wheel is allowed there, and the משנה proves nothing about sound.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest / perhaps
His garden
His ruin (an abandoned plot with plants)

steps.whatToRemember: Every source raised against רבה's view, that only a musical sound is forbidden, has been explained another way. The sick-person ברייתא is about a humming, musical sound. Clapping is banned in case he picks up a pebble. Nuts and apples are banned because of leveling holes, and the wheel because of watering a garden. None of these sources proves that a plain, non-musical sound is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא answers challenges. A ban that seems to come from one reason is explained as a separate rabbinic safeguard, so the general rule stays in place. Here that rule is רבה's view that only a musical sound is forbidden.

phrases.english: No, it is a decree
lest he draw water for his garden and for his ruin.
phrases.notes: Watering plants on שבת is a forbidden מלאכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְמַלֵּא לְגִינָּתוֹ וּלְחוּרְבָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the water-wheel משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ban (a rabbinic safeguard against watering).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wheel is banned outside the מקדש because it makes noise.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wheel is banned because a person might water his garden; this worry does not apply in the מקדש.

steps.title: אמימר permits the water wheel in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר allowed people to draw water with a wheel on שבת in מחוזא. His reasoning was that the חכמים banned it only out of concern for watering gardens and ruins, and מחוזא had neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר allowed drawing water with a wheel in מחוזא. He said: Why did the חכמים make this גזירה? Because someone might draw water for his garden or his ruin. But here there are no gardens and no ruins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a practical story. אמימר used the reason from step 30 to allow the water wheel in one specific city, מחוזא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said the wheel is banned only because a person might water his garden or his ruin. אמימר reasoned that if a place has no gardens and no ruins, that worry does not exist there. So he permitted the wheel in מחוזא, a city that was completely built up.

keyTerms.meaning: אמימר, an אמורא from a later generation
permitted, allowed
a wheel used to draw water from a well
מחוזא, a crowded, fully built-up city in Bavel
what is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: אמימר is not arguing with the גזירה from step 30. He accepts it completely. He only says that its reason does not apply in a place with no gardens or ruins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows how knowing the reason behind a גזירה can affect how widely it applies. As the next line hints, though, this approach can run into trouble in practice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reason for the wheel גזירה from step 30 and applies it to a real place where that reason does not exist.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a place with no gardens or ruins, אמימר allowed drawing water with a wheel on שבת, because the reason for the גזירה is missing.

steps.title: אמימר sees something that changes the picture
steps.stepSummary: The story starts to turn. אמימר saw people in מחוזא doing something. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once he saw that they were...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It opens the next part of the story, where אמימר observes how people actually used the wheel, and the sentence is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כיון ('once') signals that what אמימר saw will change his ruling. Even though the official reason for the גזירה seemed missing in מחוזא, real-life behavior is about to bring up a new concern.

keyTerms.meaning: once, since, as soon as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat אמימר's leniency in step 31 as the final word. This line signals that the story is about to reverse.
